tasks.short: Observe meal preparation and suggest practical alternatives

steps.what: Observe the client's meal preparation and kitchen constraints
Discuss food preferences, available equipment and manageable changes
Suggest and demonstrate alternate methods of food preparation

tasks.design: Keep observation, discussion and demonstration with the assistant. A native {DOCS} reference view could help where approved food-preparation guidance is actually consulted, but this visit boundary establishes no current lookup, written advice or case-note production to accelerate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe suggestions depend on what the client can afford, handle and accept in their own kitchen.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology removes that observation or negotiation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe preparation and avoiding advice beyond the assistant's competence.
tasks.human_edge: Notice dexterity, confidence, available utensils and the client's response to a demonstration.
tasks.altitude: The assistant continues practical support with unchanged decision rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: practical support with meal preparation depends on direct observation and discussion; documentation requirements vary by service.

assumptions: The focal boundary is a live support visit from observing preparation through practical suggestions. Shares describe a provisional work decomposition, not measured organisational time.
There is no structured input contract or proposed automation. The client supplies preferences in s2 and the assistant observes constraints in s1.

Record writes, handouts and sends were examined separately: none is established by this task statement. Do not create a meal-advice log merely to automate it. Where an actual care-plan update is required, add its first write and any real release with their own time before estimating savings.
Native reference retrieval and existing note templates should be tested against actual visit practice before adding software; neither changes the live steps here.
No incremental upkeep is incurred because no system change is proposed.
unknowns: Whether this service requires a care-plan update or written preparation instructions after the visit
Whether assistants currently consult approved guidance during this task
research_questions: Observe a visit and identify any actual first note, lookup or handout and who uses it.

already_counted.description: All observation, client discussion and demonstration remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: No introduced system or maintenance work.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 focal hours remain and upkeep is zero. A client needing repeated demonstrations retains that work too; no template or recording saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Establish which facilities the tenant needs and any access concerns
Find current laundry or playground details in the facilities directory
Inform tenants about facilities and check their understanding

tasks.design: Configure building and facility bookmarks in the existing {DOCS} directory to remove repeated navigation to the laundry or playground entry. The assistant still checks currency and accessibility and gives the explanation personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facility details may be spread over building pages or printed guidance.
tasks.enabler_now: Native bookmarks can expose the relevant existing entry without generating new advice.
tasks.still_hard: Temporary closures, individual access needs and explaining rules understandably.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise uncertainty or access barriers and adapt the explanation.
tasks.altitude: A little less directory navigation; the same tenant support responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document bookmarks can shorten retrieval of existing facility information; they do not establish whether it is current.

assumptions: The focal boundary is an in-person answer with an existing facility-directory lookup. Shares and reductions are hypotheses requiring observation, not measured baselines.

The facilities team already maintains building identifier, facility name, location, opening hours, access rules, contact and revision date in the directory. Its existing maintenance is outside this task and not a saving. No new structured feed is required: bookmarks point to original pages; missing or stale details require manual enquiry within retained s2 time.
Test native {DOCS} bookmarks first. Only repeated page navigation, estimated at 15% of s2, is removed; reading, currency checks and fallback stay.

No booking, tenant record or message send is established in this spoken branch. Add real written-message preparation and a version-bound gated send if the observed service uses that branch; no invented trailing contact log.
unknowns: Actual directory use and navigation time
Whether closure information is maintained reliably
Whether this service normally supplies written facility information
research_questions: Can a building-specific bookmark remove navigation while preserving source and revision checks?

already_counted.description: Checking directory currency and resolving missing details remain in s2.

incremental.description: Assistant checks that facility bookmarks still resolve after directory changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; only directory navigation removes 15*0.15=2.25 hours, less 0.35 upkeep gives 1.90 net. Cautious case: temporary closures require manual contact and only 0.60 hours of navigation are avoided, leaving 0.25 after the same upkeep; conversation remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Direct support remains the job; bookmarks reduce a small part of facility-information retrieval.
skills_to_grow: Check source currency and accessibility information
Distinguish practical meal support from specialist dietary advice
role.ambitious_version: No broader service is justified by these small or zero savings.
